prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1143; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a sideswipe during a lane change, and the claimant's vehicle was identified as the other car involved. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file points to damage existing before coverage began.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Responding officers and two bystanders' statements line up on the basic sequence of events.

Entry 4: Photos taken at the scene show damage consistent with the reported impact, including matching scrape height and paint transfer along the passenger side of the claimant's car. Photos confirm some details of the collision, but no independent witness has come forward to describe how the lane change happened.

Entry 5: Adjuster inspected the claimant's vehicle and found no sign of earlier damage in the affected areas. Repair estimate was requested from the body shop of the claimant's choice.

Entry 6: Claimant reported neck and lower back discomfort following the collision and was seen at an urgent care facility the same day. Medical records describe a back strain. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records we have requested so far.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided a summary of ongoing treatment. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this kind, and the reason for the extended course is still being reviewed.

Entry 8: Obtained the claimant's prior medical history through the authorization on file. No earlier injury to the same body area is known, though the records are not yet complete for the last several years.

Entry 9: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of the lane change and the impact matched what the claimant described at the scene and to the responding officer.

Entry 10: Reviewed the treating physician's notes with the medical reviewer. It is not yet clear whether the back strain was caused by this crash or by another source, and a records review is pending before any conclusion is drawn.

Entry 11: Set a follow-up to request updated treatment records and the physician's causation opinion before the next reserve review. Claim remains open pending those documents and the repair estimate.
